findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancellation blocks all remaining cancellations in the cron run
findings.body: The loop over remindersToCancel awaits client.request inside a single try/catch that wraps the whole loop, and the Prisma deletes are only executed after the loop finishes. If cancelling any one reminder fails (e.g. SendGrid error or a stale/null referenceId), the catch aborts the loop: every later reminder is never attempted, and even reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are not deleted from the DB in this run. Worse, the failing reminder stays first in the result set on subsequent runs, so it can poison every 15-minute cron invocation and workflow emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings keep being sent. Each reminder's cancellation and deletion should be isolated in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Rescheduled bookings still use immediate SendGrid cancellation, defeating the deferred-cancellation fix
findings.body: For a reschedule, deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true, which immediately POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid. Per the PR description, cancelled scheduled sends accumulate in SendGrid's scheduled_sends (capped at 100 pending cancellations) until their scheduled date, and once that cap is hit further cancellations fail and the old email is still sent. Reschedules therefore remain subject to exactly the bug this PR claims to fix for rescheduled bookings; they should be marked cancelled=true and left for the scheduleEmailReminders cron to cancel within the last hour, like the cancellation paths do.

findings.title: immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row neither deleted nor marked cancelled
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true and a referenceId exists, the function cancels the send at SendGrid and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Callers that do not subsequently cascade-delete the row (notably handleNewBooking's reschedule path, where the old booking and its reminders persist) leave a row with scheduled=true pointing at an already-cancelled batch. The stale row is only cleaned up by the cron's past-scheduledDate sweep, and any logic that later iterates the old booking's workflowReminders will try to cancel the same batch again.

findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting the promises (the same pattern is used in handleNewBooking's reschedule block, where the surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections either). The handler can return 'Booking successfully cancelled' before the cancelled=true update (or SMS cancellation/row deletion) has actually been persisted; if the serverless invocation is torn down after the response, the flag is never written and the scheduled reminder email is still sent for the cancelled booking. The cancellation promises should be collected and awaited (e.g. Promise.all over flatMap).
